## A memory system with a ceiling

Eight warps streaming, every lane on a line of its own and none read twice.

| Lines a cycle | Cycles | queued | vs none |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no ceiling | 3,416 | 0 | — |
| 32 | 3,416 | 0 | **1.00x** |
| 8 | 3,399 | 6,720 | **1.00x** |
| 2 | 3,566 | 28,800 | **1.04x** |
| 1 | 3,806 | 59,520 | **1.11x** |

## What it does to more SMs

The same sweep *Several SMs* makes, with and without a ceiling of eight lines a
cycle. Every scaling figure in this file was taken without one.

| SMs | no ceiling | vs 1 SM | 8 lines a cycle | vs 1 SM |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 83,884 | 1.00x | 83,884 | **1.00x** |
| 2 | 42,913 | 1.95x | 42,913 | **1.95x** |
| 4 | 21,366 | 3.93x | 21,366 | **3.93x** |
| 8 | 11,385 | 7.37x | 11,385 | **7.37x** |
| 16 | 9,622 | 8.72x | 9,622 | **8.72x** |
| 32 | 9,847 | 8.52x | 9,847 | **8.52x** |

The streaming warps ask for 0.60 lines a cycle and the renderer for 0.02. A
ceiling binds when it is below what a kernel asks for, and nothing else — which is
why every figure in this file stands.
